## Historical audit: S0147

**Scope.** This is chunk 3 of 3 only. Citations below refer to source **S0147**, original file `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/scene_rsi_pilot/C2/test/commons_199974832/trajectory.jsonl`. The photographs and renders are referenced, not visible in this audit; the student’s visual descriptions are not independent verification.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Line 22, `model_request`, chars [0,302306) | The requested goal was an editable reconstruction of a single indoor photograph. The student interpreted it as a woodworking shop and programmed architecture, shelving, many planes and wall tools, a workbench, kettle, bottle, trays and loose tools. This establishes multiple constructed objects, not their visibility or correctness. |
| Line 22, same range, step 1 program and result | The code grouped components such as plane cutters and handles and kettle lid, spout and bail under owners; it assigned wood-, iron-, steel- and glass-colored finishes. No image textures or physical material properties are demonstrated. Placement and rotations were programmed, but contact, part connections and pose were not geometrically tested. Step 1 returned `ok: true` and saved a render. |
| Line 22, same range, step 2 program and result | The student hypothesized that several surfaces were too bright, then reduced world strength from .45 to .14 and area-light powers from 850/650 to 230/150, retaining the scene and camera. Step 2 returned `ok: true`. The later claim that light/dark ordering improved is the student’s visual assessment, not an independently observed result. |
| Line 22, same range, step 3 program and result | The student estimated an unwanted upper empty band and shelf-spacing mismatch, then changed camera position height 2.83→2.63, target height 1.94→1.84 and lens 28→34, retaining the darker lighting. Step 3 returned `ok: true`. Its predicted framing improvement remains unverified here. |
| Line 23, `codex_session`, chars [0,4300); line 24, `model_response`, chars [0,348); line 25, `select`, chars [0,58) | The final review session was read-only, with four images supplied and no tool calls recorded. The student answered `SELECT 3`; the subsequent selection event records step 3. Selection is not proof of visual or geometric correctness. |

**Teacher input and exploration.** The visible request contains shared procedural guidance and runner feedback, including successful-render status, scheduling evidence and instructions to compare anchors. No separately identified teacher message, teacher diagnosis or teacher-proposed patch is visible in this chunk; neither teacher receipt nor adoption can be established. The student independently chose an illumination experiment followed by a camera experiment, within that guidance. The recorded final review had no tool-based exploration.

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Three executions formally returned successful renders, and step 3 was selected. This supports **operational success**, not a verified scene match or formal correctness; no algorithm failure, empty patch or technical interruption is evidenced here. Texture fidelity, actual visibility and occlusion of individual objects, support/collisions, composite integrity, shadow quality and camera match remain unresolved. The student’s estimates of shelf positions, kettle position and upper crop are hypotheses rather than measurements available to this auditor.

**Lessons.** Transferable: separate an appearance revision from a camera revision and preserve a successful fallback, while treating render status as distinct from fidelity. Task-specific: the shelf, kettle and upper-wall anchors motivated this particular camera hypothesis; their stated coordinates and lighting values should not be generalized.
